questions.question: When you see other drivers acting or reacting in anger, what should you do?

options.text: Don't make eye contact.
Don't use hand gestures.
Move away from the situation.
All of these.

questions.explanation: When other drivers are angry, stay safe by moving away from them. Don't look at them or make gestures that could anger them. Slow down, change lanes, or do whatever keeps you out of danger.

questions.question: When driving on slick roads, you should:

options.text: Take turns more slowly than usual.
Change lanes quickly.
Speed up quickly.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take turns more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, turns and curves are especially dangerous. Slow down more than you would on dry roads.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Drive around a lowered gate.
Don't worry about how many tracks are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When approaching railroad tracks, look and listen for trains. Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding can kill.
Speeding is safe if you are a skilled driver.
Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."

questions.correctAnswerText: Both "Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous" and "Speeding can kill."
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes deadlier. At speeds over 80 mph, you have almost no chance of surviving a crash. Driving much slower than other traffic is also dangerous because drivers may make unsafe moves to pass you.

questions.question: Before changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot for other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let them merge safely.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the interstate, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Don't make a last-minute turn if you miss your exit. Go to the next exit instead.

questions.question: When entering traffic from a private driveway, you must:

options.text: Yield to vehicles on the main road.
You have the right-of-way.
Only enter if there is a traffic light.
Have someone stop traffic for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles on the main road.
questions.explanation: When entering a road from a driveway, alley, or parking lot, you must yield to all vehicles already on the main road.

questions.question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the flagger's directions.
Do what other drivers do, not what the flagger says.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws, ignoring the construction zone.

questions.explanation: Follow all directions from flaggers, signs, and police in construction zones. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: One-way traffic.
Two-way left turn.
Two-way traffic.
Minimum speed limit.

questions.explanation: This sign tells you that traffic on this street goes in only one direction. You must drive in the direction the sign shows.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when large trucks, buses, and vehicles with trailers turn?

options.text: They yield to all left-turning traffic.
They back up to make room before completing the turn.
They make wide turns and may cross the centerline.
They may stop unexpectedly during the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make wide turns and may cross the centerline.
questions.explanation: Large trucks, buses, and trailers need extra space to turn. They swing wide and may cross the centerline. Do not crowd the intersection or try to pass these vehicles, especially on the right side.

questions.question: On a sidewalk or in a crosswalk, bicyclists should ride slowly and:

options.text: Not give an audible signal before passing pedestrians.
Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians.
Take the right-of-way without yielding to pedestrians.
Not need to avoid hitting a pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists can ride on a sidewalk unless local rules say otherwise. Bicyclists must always yield to pedestrians on sidewalks and in crosswalks.

questions.question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle from a friend, you should:

options.text: Not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide from your friend that you do not know the vehicle well.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take time before driving to learn how to operate the vehicle and where all equipment is located.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take time before driving to learn how to operate the vehicle and where all equipment is located.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, spend a few minutes learning where and how to use the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow while you are driving, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicles ahead.
Be cautious around all other vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your following distance on wet, cold roads because your vehicle needs more distance to stop on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing with no visible train, you must stop if:

options.text: A stop sign is posted.
A crossing gate is lowered.
The crossing lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if the lights are flashing, the gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger tells you to stop, or a train is visible or too close to cross safely. Never race a train.

questions.question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely:

options.text: A deaf person.
Someone doing a traffic study.
A blind person.
None of the above.

questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, as they are likely blind.

questions.question: If you are involved in a crash, you should:

options.text: Stop at or near the crash scene.
Not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of wrecked vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Stop at or near the crash. Move your vehicle out of traffic if possible. Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes because another vehicle could hit you. Turn off the engines in damaged vehicles.

questions.question: Anything that makes you ____ could cause a crash.

options.text: Take your eyes off the road
Take your hands off the wheel
Take your attention away from driving
All of the above

questions.explanation: A distraction is anything that takes your attention away from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or takes your hands off the wheel.

questions.question: Distracted driving can be caused by:

options.text: Eating, drinking, or smoking.
Talking or texting on a cell phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions per mile. You must focus fully on driving. Any extra task can be a dangerous distraction.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a low-speed crash.
Always make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints before driving. Seat belts greatly reduce your chance of injury or death in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit properly restrained in a rear seat. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with a front airbag.

questions.question: What does alcohol do?

options.text: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
Puts you to sleep.
Wakes you up.
Improves your judgment.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reflexes and reaction time.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and reduces your driving skills. It slows your reaction time and impairs your judgment.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?

options.text: It slows your reaction time.
It gives you false confidence.
It impairs your thinking.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time, coordination, and balance. It also impairs your vision and ability to judge distance.

questions.question: What should you do before starting your car?

options.text: Check that only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Check that only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Check that only children have buckled their seat belts.
Check that all passengers have buckled their seat belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that all passengers have buckled their seat belts.
questions.explanation: Always buckle your seat belt first. Then make sure all your passengers buckle theirs before you start driving.

questions.question: How can you best avoid hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires in good condition.
Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
Avoid standing water and puddles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On wet roads, your car takes longer to stop and may skid during turns. Do not use cruise control on wet or icy roads. Reduce your speed and drive carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Honk at oncoming traffic.
Keep your speed the same.
Speed up to avoid traffic.
Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if safe, to let traffic in.
questions.explanation: When you have two or more lanes, make room for traffic entering the road. Move over one lane if the lane next to you is empty.
